text: Good evening. I'm Dana, I've lived in Ward 2 for twenty years, and I strongly support the new community garden because my block has no green space at all. Please vote yes and fund the water connection.

As the city budget director, I must formally oppose this amendment. It cuts the transit subsidy by fifteen percent and forces service reductions on the two busiest crosstown lines. I recommend rejecting it.

I'm Priya, a resident of Ward 4, and I'm not here to take a position for or against the parking meter policy. I simply ask staff to publish the raw sensor data and extend the comment period so merchants can review the numbers.

As a homeowner on Birchwood Lane, my view is mixed. I support building a dog park in principle, but as drafted the plan has no drainage redesign and no maintenance budget, so I cannot support this exact site without those fixes.

I'm the parks superintendent, and our division fully supports the tree protection ordinance. Canopy cover has fallen sharply and the rule gives staff a permitting tool before removal rather than a fine afterward.

The following anonymous comment was submitted online with no contact information. I oppose the roundabout at Fifth and Grove because emergency response times were never modeled for snow conditions. Please keep the signal.
Written submission, identity not verified. I am not saying yes or no to the drainage project; I only ask that my dated flooding observations be entered into the technical file before anyone decides.

As planning director I have a mixed recommendation. I support the land-use direction near the rail station, but the environmental assessment is Phase One only, so I cannot recommend unconditional approval tonight.
